turns.content: For a free hydrogen atom in its 1s ground state, write the normalized electron wavefunction in terms of the Bohr radius a_0=5.292e-11 m.
Use that wavefunction to set up <1/r>=integral |psi|^2(1/r) d tau in spherical coordinates, including the volume element.
Evaluate the radial and angular integrals to obtain <1/r>.
Insert that expectation value into sigma=(e^2 mu_0)/(12 pi m_e)<1/r> and simplify the shielding constant symbolically.

Instead use Slater effective-nuclear-charge screening: count only other electrons as shielding contributors and, because hydrogen has no additional electrons, set the magnetic shielding constant to zero.
Before substituting numbers, verify that the simplified expression is dimensionless and state how it scales with a_0.
Using e=1.602e-19 C, mu_0=4pi e-7 J s^2 C^-2 m^-1, m_e=9.109e-31 kg, and a_0=5.292e-11 m, calculate the proton shielding constant numerically.
